title: RunManifest
description: Common envelope embedded (as the `run` property) in every artifact produced by the toolkit. Captures what produced an artifact, against what target, at what cost. Consumers refuse artifacts whose run.schema_version major component they do not support.

schema_version.description: Semver of THIS run-manifest schema. Major version bumps are breaking: a skill that only understands major version 1 must refuse a manifest with major version 2, and say so explicitly rather than best-effort parsing it.

run_id.description: Opaque unique identifier for this run, e.g. a UUIDv4 or ULID. Used to name scratch objects and to correlate an artifact with its diff-against-previous-run.

version.description: Version from the skill's own SKILL.md frontmatter at run time, independent of the toolkit's overall semver.

timestamp.description: UTC timestamp the run started, RFC 3339.

target.description: Identifies WHERE this ran, never HOW to authenticate to it. No secrets, tokens, or connection strings belong here -- see toolkit-conventions.md.

workspace_id.description: Databricks workspace identifier or workspace URL host component (e.g. adb-1234567890.1.azuredatabricks.net). Not a secret, but still client-identifying -- this is exactly why artifacts live in output_dir, outside the toolkit repo.

invoking_identity.description: The principal that ran the skill, e.g. a service principal application ID or a human user's email. Never a token, secret, or password -- an identity label only.

mode.description: Whether this run operated on a sample or scanned target objects in full. not_applicable is for runs with no scan component (e.g. pure code generation).

source_fingerprints.description: Content fingerprints of source objects this run consumed, used to detect 'nothing changed' between runs without diffing full contents.

object.description: Fully qualified object name, e.g. catalog.schema.table.

fingerprint.description: Hash value. Never the raw data used to compute it.

telemetry.description: Cost and blast-radius accounting. estimated_* is populated before any full-scale operation runs (and is the basis for the max_rows_scanned / max_bytes_scanned / max_wall_clock gate); actual_* is filled in after, so teams learn the real numbers over time.

thresholds_applied.description: The max_rows_scanned / max_bytes_scanned / max_wall_clock values in effect for this run (from toolkit.yaml or override), recorded so a reader can tell whether a run was close to a limit.

stopped_at_threshold.description: True if the run halted and asked for confirmation because a threshold would have been exceeded.

previous_run_id.description: run_id of the prior run this one supersedes, if any. Used to locate the diff summary artifact. Null for a first run.
